summary: Backend (site/config, send-otp demo, verify-otp partner) all pass. Frontend welcome + partner login flow (welcome-login-btn -> login-phone-input -> send-otp-btn -> verify-otp-btn) works and lands on the partner dashboard with the full bottom tab bar (Dashboard, Job Request, Active Job, Wallet & With..., More). Dark-mode core fix VERIFIED: after tapping the header theme-toggle on the dashboard and navigating in-app via More -> Rewards & Challenges / My Availability / Starter Kit, all three screens (plus dashboard and the More sheet itself) render uniformly with a dark page background (rgb(11,17,32) / rgb(30,41,59)). The screen intermittency the user reported is not reproducible in-app anymore.

ui_bugs.issue: The manual dark-mode override is not persisted (no AsyncStorage/localStorage). On a full page reload / direct-URL open the override resets to admin default_mode (currently 'light') and userPinned ref resets to false, so dark mode is lost. Reproduces by: toggle dark on dashboard -> hard-refresh or open /(partner)/partner/rewards directly -> page renders in light. Not blocking for the reported bug (in-app nav is uniform now), but users who refresh/re-open the app will see the theme snap back to admin default_mode.

The very first click on the theme toggle right after login is occasionally a no-op (icon and background do not change); the second click works. Suspected race between the initial useEffect syncing forcedMode and the click's setOverride. Second click reliably flips the theme. Manageable in real use but slightly confusing UX.

action_items: Consider persisting the user's manual theme override to AsyncStorage/localStorage (e.g. key 'themeOverride') and hydrating it in ThemeProvider's initial useState so dark mode survives page reloads / cold starts.
Investigate the 'first-click no-op' on the theme-toggle after login (possibly re-run useEffect that resets override, or capture setOverride inside a ref so pinMode is stable).
critical_code_review_comments: src/theme.ts: `toggleMode` is recreated every render inside ThemeProvider but the value object is memoized on `[mode, brand.*]` — the toggle callback is not part of the deps, which is fine because it re-runs when mode changes. However, `pinMode` sets a ref synchronously AND setState — if forcedMode is not yet resolved on first render, the subsequent useEffect can still overwrite override before userPinned=true is observed (this is likely the cause of the intermittent first-click no-op).
app/_layout.tsx: mode derivation on line 69 collapses 'system' to undefined which is correct, but there is no persistence layer for user pins — see UI bug above.
rewards.tsx / availability.tsx / starter-kit.tsx correctly consume useTheme() -> colors.background so they respect the provider — no per-screen fix needed.

success_rate.frontend: 100% (core dark-mode fix), with 2 residual issues noted above

context_for_next_testing_agent: The dark-mode-race-on-late-forcedMode fix in /app/frontend/src/theme.ts (useEffect syncing forcedMode + userPinned ref) is verified working. In-app navigation to Rewards & Challenges (via more-incentives), My Availability (more-availability) and Starter Kit (more-starterkit) all render uniformly dark after tapping theme-toggle on the dashboard. Two residual issues remain (not blocking the reported bug): (a) dark override is not persisted across full-page reloads / direct URL opens — the theme snaps back to admin default_mode ('light') because ThemeProvider's `override` is only in-memory; (b) the very first click on theme-toggle right after login is occasionally a no-op (second click reliably flips). If main agent wants to fully close the user's complaint they should persist `override` to localStorage/AsyncStorage.
rca of the issue: Original race: ThemeProvider was initialised with override = forcedMode (undefined at first mount because /api/site/config had not resolved). Once site config resolved, forcedMode became the admin 'default_mode' but override was never re-synced -> some screens still saw the stale value and rendered light while others rendered dark depending on when they first mounted. E1's fix adds a useEffect syncing setOverride(forcedMode) whenever forcedMode changes, gated by a userPinned ref so a manual toggle wins. Verified: dashboard + rewards + availability + starter-kit all render dark after one toggle when navigated in-app. Remaining gap: userPinned is a ref (in-memory only), so a page reload/cold start loses the user's manual choice.
